description:
Four satellite imagery panels display an urban area on 2020-02-15, comparing Sentinel-2 (S2) data at 10 m and 2.5 m spatial resolutions, including zoomed views. The x and y axes show coordinate values, ranging from approximately 538400 to 538900 and 4747000 to 4748200, respectively, for the overview panels, and narrower ranges for the zoomed views. Green circles highlight specific features in all four panels.

The top-left panel is labelled "S2 10 m 2020-02-15" and shows an overview of the urban area at 10 m resolution, with a 200 m scale bar. The top-right panel, "S2 2.5 m 2020-02-15", displays the same area at 2.5 m resolution, also with a 200 m scale bar.

The bottom-left panel, "S2 10 m (zoom)", provides a magnified view of a central pentagonal building and surrounding structures at 10 m resolution, with a 50 m scale bar. The bottom-right panel, "S2 2.5 m (zoom)", presents the zoomed area at 2.5 m resolution, also with a 50 m scale bar.

The comparison clearly illustrates the significantly higher level of detail and clarity achieved with 2.5 m resolution imagery compared to 10 m, enabling better identification of urban morphology, individual buildings, roads, and land cover features. This enhanced resolution is crucial for detailed Land Cover / Land Use (LCLU) mapping and validation processes, particularly for complex environments like urban areas or those within Natura 2000 (N2K) sites where high accuracy is required for Copernicus Land Monitoring Service (CLMS) products.
